Title: Mother, child get 2-day remand as police probe stray dog operation assault
Article:
MUAR: Police have opened two investigation papers into a mother and her child over the assault of a Muar Municipal Council (MPM) enforcement officer during an operation to catch stray dogs.
The incident allegedly occurred here at Taman Bintang Emas, Bukit Pasir, two days ago.
Muar police chief Assistant Commissioner Raiz Mukhliz Azman Aziz said the suspects, aged 24 and 52, were being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of their duties and Section 353 of the same code for using criminal force against a public servant.
He said the duo had been remanded for two days at the Muar Magistrate's Court from yesterday to assist in investigations.
"Investigations found that the incident occurred at about 5.45am two days ago while MPM enforcement officers were conducting an integrated operation to catch stray dogs in the area.

Title: Anwar calls for pondok schools to be upgraded to university level
Article:
PASIR MAS: Pondok institutions should be strengthened and upgraded to university level to ensure they remain relevant to the changing needs of society.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the traditional Islamic education system should not be abandoned but adapted to current developments while preserving its role in safeguarding the Muslim community's faith and character.
He said pondok institutions had long served as a stronghold for the Muslim community, particularly in protecting its faith, moral values and knowledge.
"These institutions can be transformed and improved, but we must ensure their education system progresses to a higher level, including university status.
"We must also master new areas of knowledge, particularly in preaching and education, if we want to move forward and prevent our country from falling behind," he said.
He was speaking after performing Maghrib prayers with more than 200 residents at Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah near Pondok Lubuk Tapah here.
Anwar said Islamic educational institutions must adapt to changing circumstances while continuing to uphold the principles and guidance of Islamic scholars.
He also urged those involved in managing pondok institutions to make full use of the knowledge taught there and ensure it benefited the wider community.
Anwar is on a one-day visit to Kelantan.
Pondok institutions are traditional Islamic schools in Malaysia that provide religious education, often in a residential setting
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 181 undocumented migrants arrested in Chow Kit raid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 181 undocumented migrants were arrested during an Immigration Department raid at Pasar Raja Bot, Chow Kit.
The operation, which began at 9.40am, involved about 200 Immigration officers and personnel who surrounded the area, a popular spot among foreigners, particularly Indonesians.
Immigration Department deputy director-general (Operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli said 512 people were checked during Ops Mega Bersepadu.
Those arrested included 106 Indonesian men and 41 women and children.
The others comprised 20 Bangladeshi men, three Indian men, five Nepali men, one Pakistani man and five people of other nationalities, including a child.
The 181 detainees comprised 136 men and 45 women, aged between 10 and 55. They were taken to the Bukit Jalil Immigration Depot.
Lokman said the location was among 224 hotspots nationwide frequented by undocumented migrants, particularly Indonesians.
The integrated operation involved 264 officers and personnel from the Immigration Department, Kuala Lumpur City Hall, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, the National Registration Department, the Fire and Rescue Department and the police.
"Foreigners used various methods to avoid arrest, including hiding on rooftops, but the use of drones enabled them to be detected," he said at a press conference.
Chow Kit is a busy commercial area in central Kuala Lumpur, known for its wet market, wholesale trade and large migrant community.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police officer held over RM3,000 bribe to settle family fight case
Article:
SEREMBAN: A police officer was arrested for allegedly taking a RM3,000 bribe from a couple to drop action over a fight involving their family member.
The man, in his 30s, was arrested at the district police headquarters at about 10pm yesterday, a source said.
The source said the bribe was sought as an inducement to refrain from taking action over the matter.
"It was in exchange for not taking action over a fight involving a family member of a couple," the source said today.
Preliminary investigations found that the offence took place on Oct 29 during an initial investigation involving the couple.
The suspect was remanded for four days until Tuesday by Magistrate Nurul Azuin Mohd Talhah following an application by the MACC at the Seremban Magistrates' Court 2.
Negri Sembilan MACC director Awgkok Ahmad Taufik Putra Awg Ismail confirmed the arrest when contacted, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 17(a) of the MACC Act 2009.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PM recalls late pondok founder's advice, encouragement
Article:
PASIR MAS: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was visibly moved as he recalled his close relationship with the late founder of Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah, Abdullah Abdul Rahman, during a gathering with about 200 congregants tonight.
Anwar spent more than 10 minutes sharing his personal experiences and memories of the late religious scholar, whom he said had played an important role in encouraging and strengthening his resolve more than 20 years ago.
Anwar said he was deeply touched by his visit to the religious institution today as he continued to hold the late Abdullah in high regard and had always prayed for him.
"Although circumstances have changed and my position has changed, I will not change.
"When I visited this madrasah more than 20 years ago, the late Abdullah gave me a lot of advice, encouragement and confidence in myself," he said.
Anwar said although the late Abdullah was known for being strict in his teaching, he had always been generous in offering advice and support.
He said the late scholar's encouragement had left a lasting impression on him, particularly during challenging periods of his life.
"That is why I felt deeply touched when I arrived here earlier. I remembered how a great religious scholar had supported me and contributed so much to my journey," he said.
Anwar said he hoped the legacy and struggles of the late Abdullah would continue to be upheld and elevated, particularly through efforts to strengthen the role of pondok institutions and Islamic education.
The Prime Minister is on a one day visit to Kelantan today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Sultan of Selangor contracts Influenza A, state ceremony postponed
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah is unwell after contracting Influenza A, the Selangor Royal Office said today.
In a statement, Istana Alam Shah said the infection was confirmed by his personal physicians, Datuk Dr Anuar Onah and Datuk Dr Tan Hui Meng.
"Symptoms of the infection were first detected on Friday morning (yesterday), when His Highness developed a high fever and general body weakness.
"Based on their assessment, His Highness may have contracted the infection while attending public functions and interacting with members of the public, including in open spaces.
"Alhamdulillah, His Highness's health is gradually improving, although he is still experiencing a fever," the statement said tonight.
The royal physicians have advised Sultan Sharafuddin to rest and refrain from attending any functions for five to seven days to allow him to make a full recovery.
Following the development, the Istiadat Menjunjung Duli and the Selangor State Honours Conferment Ceremony, scheduled to be held tomorrow (Nov 1) in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebrations of the Sultan's reign, have been postponed to Nov 7.
"All parties involved are requested to take note of the change in date. Their cooperation and attention are greatly appreciated.
The statement also called on the public to pray for the Sultan's speedy recovery and continued good health.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar announces RM200mil increase in business grants under Skim Usahawan Bangkit
Article:
KOTA BARU: The Federal Government will increase grants under the Skim Usahawan Bangkit by RM200 million next year to help small entrepreneurs expand their businesses and boost their earnings.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said even modest allocations could make a significant difference when channelled directly to businesses in need.
He said relatively small purchases, such as affordable refrigerators to preserve stock, could prevent losses and generate thousands of ringgit in additional monthly income.
"Sometimes the expenditure is only RM5,000, RM3,000 or even RM1,800, but it can bring good returns.
"I have seen businesses that simply need a small, inexpensive refrigerator to keep their goods from spoiling. That alone can increase their returns by thousands of ringgit a month," he said.
Anwar was speaking at the launch of the Skim Usahawan Bangkit Negeri Kelantan here yesterday.
He said the government would continue monitoring the needs of entrepreneurs and provide assistance wherever possible.
He also thanked Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud and the state government for their cooperation, saying any issues could be resolved through discussion.
"If there are problems, we will discuss them amicably," he said.

Title: Fahmi extends condolences over death of Mata Ayer assemblyman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has expressed his condolences to the family of Mata Ayer assemblyman Wan Badariah Wan Saad, who died today.
"My deepest condolences to the entire family of the deceased, as well as to her friends and fellow comrades," he said in a Facebook post.
Wan Badariah died
at Tuanku Fauziah Hospital in Kangar at 4.26pm.
She won the Mata Ayer seat under the Perikatan Nasional ticket in the 15th General Election with a majority of 2,021 votes.

Title: Chicken killed by electric current may have reached Muslim eateries
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Chicken suspected of having been killed by electric current before slaughter at a processing plant raided in Puchong yesterday may have been supplied to Muslim-owned restaurants.
Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said preliminary investigations found that the premises used the water-bath stunning method, with excessively high electric voltage believed to have caused the chickens to die before slaughter.
He said the council was concerned that the chicken supply had reached Muslim-owned restaurants.
"How can we allow these irresponsible people to do such a thing?" he said.
He urged Muslims, restaurant operators and food business owners to check the source of their chicken supplies and ensure that the food they serve is halal.
"If they (restaurants) do not care where their chicken supplies come from, (I am worried) this will cause Muslims to consume non-halal food," he said after the Selangor State-Level 2026 Ahlus Sunnah Wal Jamaah Fundamental Declaration programme.
Salehuddin said preliminary investigations found that the premises were believed to be Muslim-owned and had been operating for a long time.
He said the premises had been ordered to close for two weeks to facilitate investigations, adding that Mais, through the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais), would continue conducting integrated operations with other government agencies.
More than
6.5 tonnes of raw chicken
suspected of being processed without complying with Islamic slaughtering and halal certification requirements were seized during the raid.
Twelve Bangladeshi and Pakistani men believed to be involved in the slaughtering and processing activities were also detained during Ops Taring Chiller.
The operation involved the police, Jais, the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim), the Department of Environment and the Petaling Health Office.
Under Islamic slaughtering requirements, chickens must be alive at the time of slaughter, with a sharp knife used to sever the throat and major blood vessels. Electrical stunning is permitted under halal standards only if it does not kill the poultry before slaughter.

Title: BN to focus on candidates, policies in Melaka election
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional will not resort to smear campaigns in the Melaka election, focusing instead on its candidates, service records, manifesto pledges and solutions for voters.
Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said voters should assess candidates based on their capabilities, experience and plans to take the state forward.
"We want to secure a mandate based on our own strengths, rather than by tearing others down. The people of Melaka deserve to make their choice based on facts, not slander or hatred," she said in a statement.
Azalina said candidates, party workers and supporters should campaign fairly, comply with election rules and avoid provocations involving race, religion and royalty.
She also called on Umno's information machinery, including its Wanita, Youth and Puteri wings, to strengthen digital campaigning, noting that 43.6 per cent of Melaka voters were aged between 21 and 40.
"Our communication approach must be more dynamic, creative and closer to young voters. Ensure that digital spaces are filled with accurate information, engaging content and factual, measured explanations," she said.
"Do not be easily influenced by unusually high numbers of likes, comments or shares. Check the sources, examine the facts and think before sharing."
Melaka's election
campaign began today
following nominations, with 79 candidates vying for all 28 state seats.
Polling is set for Nov 14, following a 14-day campaign period, while early voting is scheduled for Nov 10.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar allocates RM200,000 for madrasah restoration
Article:
PASIR MAS: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today handed over a RM200,000 mock cheque for the maintenance and restoration of Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah at Pondok Lubuk Tapah here.
The allocation was part of the 2026 Maintenance and Restoration Project for Islamic Educational Institutions in Kelantan.
The mock cheque was received by the madrasah's chairman, Datuk Dr Luqman Abdullah.
The financial assistance is expected to support maintenance and repair works at the religious institution.
Anwar also spent about 30 minutes at Luqman's home before performing the Maghrib prayers.
The Prime Minister was on his one day working visit to Kelantan.
Later tonight, he is expected to attend another programme called 'Sebarkan Salam' at the state mosque in Kota Baru.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK PM 'open' to slavery apology but not reparations
Article:
LONDON: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Saturday he was "open" to the UK issuing a formal apology for its role in the transatlantic slave trade, but ruled out financial reparations.
The Labour leader made the remarks days before attending a Commonwealth leaders summit in Antigua and Barbuda, as King Charles III tours the Caribbean.
"I want to express my sorrow and regret for the pain and suffering of so many millions and to recognise the way it still shapes our world today," Burnam wrote in the Guardian newspaper.
The transatlantic slave trade was a "brutal and barbaric violation" of the rights of those enslaved, he said.
The British premier added his government wanted a "structured dialogue with those affected."
"Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process and I am open to them."
The king is due to address the Commonwealth summit, which runs from November 1 to 4.
Britain's central role in slavery and the treatment of people in its former colonies has loomed over the 77-year-old monarch's Caribbean tour.
In the Bahamas on Tuesday, Charles acknowledged  "the great suffering of the past" during the first leg of his visit.
Britain has never formally apologised for slavery or agreed to pay reparations.
Burnham again rejected financial compensation, writing: "I do not believe that is the right answer."
"I do not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played no personal part."
Britain profited for centuries from colonialism and the slave trade. In 1833, parliament passed a law to abolish slavery.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 17 held after reported fight at Ampang flat
Article:
AMPANG: Police have detained 17 people to assist in investigations into a reported fight at Flat Lembah Jaya.
Ampang Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said a patrol car unit was dispatched to the scene after receiving an emergency call at 2.07am.
"Officers sent to the location found no fight taking place, but a group of people had gathered there.
"Seventeen people were detained to assist in investigations under Section 148 of the Penal Code. The reason for their gathering is still being investigated," he said in a statement today.
He said two suspects had been remanded for two days, while the remaining 15 were remanded for three days to assist in further investigations.
Videos circulating on social media showed a group gathering in the Lembah Jaya area, while other posts included claims of a fight there.

Title: 2 women held after Muar dog-catching operation
Article:
MUAR: Two women have been arrested following an incident involving a Muar Municipal Council enforcement officer during a stray dog-catching operation in a residential area yesterday.
Muar district police chief Assistant Commissioner Raiz Mukhliz Azman Aziz confirmed that police had received a report on the case and said the two women were arrested to assist in investigations.
The incident occurred when the officer tried to stop the two women, who were believed to have released dogs caught during the operation despite being given a verbal warning.
A scuffle broke out, causing the officer to fall.
The officer subsequently lodged a police report.
Several photographs of the incident later went viral on social media, showing a man wearing a Muar Municipal Council vest lying on the ground.
The incident drew angry reactions from social media users, with some calling on the council to take action against the women involved.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jom Heboh carnival draws bigger crowds on second day
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The second day of the Jom Heboh Carnival (KHJ) Johor Baru 2026 at Angsana Johor Baru Mall here continued to draw large crowds today.
Residents from Johor and neighbouring Singapore took advantage of the weekend to visit the event.
Visitors arrived at Padang B as early as 9am, with the crowd growing towards late morning and early afternoon. The turnout is expected to remain strong until tonight.
Housewife Shalizawati Sapar, 44, from Batu Pahat, said she brought her four children to the carnival as a reward for completing their school examinations.
"My children love coming to the carnival. They ask to go every year. When they told me the carnival would be held in Johor Baru this weekend, I immediately thought of bringing them, especially since their examinations had just ended.
"It was the perfect time to reward them with an outing. My husband was also off today, so we left Batu Pahat early this morning.
"We visit KJH to shop for affordable goods, while my children enjoy the Tonton booths because of the various activities. They are also excited whenever they get the chance to meet television personalities and celebrities," she said, adding that she hoped the carnival would continue to be held annually.
KJH Johor Baru 2026 features various attractions, including sales booths, performances by local artistes, family-oriented activities and offers on a wide range of daily essentials.
Recognised by the Malaysia Book of Records (MBOR) as the "Longest Running Outdoor Carnival", the three-day event began yesterday and will end tomorrow.
Media Prima Omnia chief operating officer Datuk Efendi Omar said favourable weather today had encouraged more visitors to spend time at the carnival, expressing hope that the strong turnout would continue until tomorrow.
"The weather today has been very favourable. The response has been extraordinary and beyond expectations. Most visitors are here with their families, and we hope this momentum continues until this evening and tomorrow.
"We will continue to offer various exciting activities for visitors. Tonight, we will host a concert featuring a line-up of popular artistes," he said.

Title: 18 Taiwanese held in Kuala Lumpur scam syndicate raid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have dismantled an international call centre syndicate that used Kuala Lumpur as a base to scam victims overseas.
Eighteen Taiwanese were arrested after being found impersonating law enforcement officers.
The raid was conducted by the Dang Wangi district Commercial Crime Investigation Division two days ago.
Dang Wangi police chief Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said those detained were 17 men and a woman, aged between 19 and 43.
"Police also seized 69 mobile phones, five laptops and two Hong Kong police uniforms.
"The items seized helped uncover the syndicate's modus operandi. Based on the items recovered, the syndicate is suspected of carrying out scams by impersonating Hong Kong police officers and targeting victims in Hong Kong," he said.
He said investigations found that the group used local internet facilities to carry out its activities.
"The syndicate used internet access to conduct online scams and had been operating for the past five months.
"All those detained have been remanded for four days until Nov 2 to assist investigations under Sections 420 and 511 of the Penal Code," he said.

Title: Kimono-clad pets blessed at Japan festival lacking enough kids
Article:
TOKYO: Chanting and swishing a wooden wand, a Japanese priest blessed a cat, a shiba inu and several Yorkshire terriers at a shrine in Tokyo on Saturday, in a rite usually reserved for children.
The annual "Shichi-Go-San" festival literally means "Seven-Five-Three" and traditionally allows families to celebrate the growth of their children at those ages.
But with Japan's population in decline, more and more worshippers are bringing beloved animals to the event instead.
"I came here to pray for my pet's healthy growth and well-being," Shoko Kodama, a 46-year-old doctor, told AFP at Ichigaya Kamegaoka Hachimangu, a Shinto shrine in the capital.
The 46-year-old doctor said she had spent two months hand-crafting a bespoke, bright-red kimono for her cat, a five-year-old British shorthair called Amber.
"This little one is like my child," she said. "Just having her around makes all the unpleasant things in life melt away."
Outside the shrine, other pet owners dressed their fluffy companions in colourful kimonos and posed them for photos to mark the special occasion.
They then brought them into the inner sanctuary, where the priest, Kenji Kaji, performed a purification rite with a wand decorated with white paper streamers.
He told AFP the role of pets in people's lives had shifted as "the family structure has changed" in Japan, which is grappling with an ageing population and a low birth rate.
"I think the number of instances where people who don't have children, or have finished raising them, and welcome a dog or cat as a member of the family has been increasing," Kaji said.
Kaji's shrine has been accepting around 400 families for each festival since the early 2000s, due to demand from pet owners.
Miyu Shiro, the 23-year-old owner of two Yorkshire terriers, said marking the event with her dogs "feels perfectly natural."
"They're part of our family," she said, as she snapped photos of her pups, neatly combed and wearing flower-shaped hair clips.
Data in June showed that Japan's fertility rate fell again last year to a record low, underscoring the demographic crisis gnawing at the world's fourth-largest economy.
With a median age of 49.9 years, Japan also has the second-oldest population in the world, after the tiny city-state of Monaco, according to the World Bank.
Koichi Ohara, 57, who attended the festival with his wife and friends, said his three Chihuahuas gave him "unconditional love."
"They're more affectionate than human children. They listen to what we say too," he laughed, adding that he had three kids.
"Just like us humans, I hope they can live long and in peace."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Thailand to finalise Sungai Golok project to solve Kelantan, southern Thailand floods
Article:
KOTA BARU: Malaysia and Thailand are expected to finalise negotiations on the Sungai Golok estuary project within a month to help mitigate flooding in Kelantan and southern Thailand.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he had had two rounds of discussions with the Thai government, including with its new prime minister, to expedite efforts to resolve the issue.
He said maintaining good relations with neighbouring countries was crucial to ensuring smooth cooperation, particularly in addressing cross-border issues and promoting peace.
"I have had discussions twice with Thailand, including with its new prime minister, to expedite the matter.
"This is why we need to maintain good relations with our neighbours to ensure that cooperation can proceed smoothly," he said.
He was speaking at the launch of the Skim Usahawan Bangkit Negeri Kelantan here today.
Also present was Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.
Anwar said the project involved addressing erosion, as well as widening and deepening the river to improve water flow and reduce flooding.
He said resolving the issue at the Sungai Golok estuary would require close cooperation between the Malaysian and Thai governments.
"I hope we can finalise the matter within a month to reduce the impact of floods in Kelantan and southern Thailand," he said.
He also expressed appreciation to the Kelantan government, particularly the state secretary, for expediting the land acquisition process to facilitate the project.
Anwar said he hoped the initiative would usher in a new chapter of development for Rantau Panjang, which had been affected by recurring floods.
He said he would hold further discussions with the Thai government within the next month to ensure progress.
The prime minister was on a one-day working visit to Kelantan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PWD assistance gets largest share of Women's Ministry's 2027 budget
Article:
KUCHING: Assistance for people with disabilities (PWD) has received the largest allocation under the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry's 2027 Budget.
Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said RM1.5 billion of the RM3.3 billion allocated to the ministry would go towards assistance for PWD, benefiting more than 300,000 recipients.
"Among the improvements introduced is an increase in the allowance for bedridden PWD and chronically ill patients from RM500 to RM600 a month.
"Eligibility for the Disabled Workers' Allowance has also been expanded to individuals earning up to RM2,000 to ensure more people benefit from government assistance," she said in her speech at the ministry's Santun Kasih 2026 event here today.
Nancy said Budget 2027 provided an important direction for strengthening welfare, social protection and the empowerment of the people, particularly the ministry's target groups.
She said the government had also allocated RM1.3 billion for elderly assistance and the care sector, which was expected to benefit nearly 200,000 recipients.
"Besides financial assistance, the government plans to establish two National Integrated Care Centres of Excellence (NICE) in Sarawak and Penang to strengthen facilities and care services for senior citizens.
"The service tax rate for elderly care services will also be reduced from eight to six per cent effective Jan 1, 2027," she said.
Assistance for children would also be increased to RM250 a month for those aged six and below, and RM200 a month for those aged between seven and 18.
She said the move was aimed at strengthening support for families in meeting basic needs while safeguarding children's development.
Nancy said women's empowerment would also be prioritised through the RM200 million Geran Sejahtera Madani grant, targeting 40,000 recipients, particularly to help them obtain equipment and training to generate income.
"Other measures include expanding tax relief for postnatal care services and improving maternity leave facilities for civil servants to support mothers' well-being," she said.
The Fertility Treatment Assistance and Infertility Advocacy Programme (BuAi) would also be expanded to benefit 2,000 couples, alongside the expansion of men's wellness services by the National Population and Family Development Board.
"All these initiatives complement the country's care economy agenda and strengthen the implementation of the Malaysia Care Strategic Framework and Action Plan 2026-2030.
"The ministry is committed to ensuring every allocation benefits the people, while expanding access to quality and affordable care services, strengthening support for families and creating economic and employment opportunities in the sector," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar says helping underprivileged will not impoverish country
Article:
KOTA BARU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said helping the underprivileged would not impoverish the country, but misconduct and poor governance could weaken and destroy it.
He said the government remained committed to assisting the poor and vulnerable while maintaining sound financial management.
This was reflected in the decision to raise civil servants' salaries, despite the move carrying an estimated cost of RM18 billion in 2026.
Anwar said cost-of-living assistance allocated this year amounted to RM16 billion, but the commitments would not burden the country.
He was speaking at the launch of the Skim Usahawan Bangkit Negeri Kelantan here today.
Anwar is on a one-day tour of Kelantan, with programmes focused on meeting the people.
He said the government would continue prioritising assistance for the lowest-income groups, particularly those in the B40 category, as outlined in Budget 2027.
The government was also focused on empowering small entrepreneurs, particularly women, through various assistance programmes.
In Kelantan, the Sejati Madani programme for entrepreneurs had received about 4,000 applications, of which 440 had been approved.
Anwar said the government would continue approving the remaining applications, noting that most applicants were women.
He said assistance programmes in Kelantan would place greater emphasis on empowering women, citing their track record in managing small businesses and repaying financing.
Drawing on his experience with Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia, he said about 99 per cent of its female borrowers made repayments, while male borrowers tended to take slightly longer.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mata Ayer assemblyman Wan Badariah dies at 50
Article:
KANGAR: Mata Ayer assemblyman Wan Badariah Wan Saad has died. She was 50.
Perlis Pas information chief Mohamad Zahid Ibrahim confirmed her death in a social media post.
He said Wan Badariah died at Tuanku Fauziah Hospital at 4.26pm.
In May 2024, it was reported that she had been treated for complications from a thyroid condition.
She later recovered and resumed her duties.
Under the previous state administration, Wan Badariah served as state tourism committee chairman.
A lawyer by profession, she was Perlis Pas' first female candidate.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pregnant mother hides behind counter as sword-wielding robber strikes jewellery shop
Article:
PETALING JAYA: A pregnant mother of three hid behind a counter in fear as a sword-wielding robber struck a jewellery shop in Damansara Damai yesterday.
Yani, who is in her 40s and three months pregnant, was working at the dessert shop next door when she heard a commotion.
"I heard a commotion and immediately hid behind the counter because I was frightened and did not know what was happening.
"It was only after the man had left that I heard the jewellery shop workers screaming 'robber, robber,' she said when met at the scene today.
Yani, who has worked at the dessert shop for just two months, said she never expected such an incident to happen there.
She eventually gathered enough courage to look outside and caught a glimpse of the suspect leaving the scene.
"He was wearing a long black raincoat, black pants and a helmet.
"What surprised me was that he was not running. He was just walking away," she said.
Yani said it all happened within minutes.
She said she later spoke to workers at the jewellery shop and learnt that the robber had been armed with a sharp object resembling a samurai sword, measuring between two and three feet long.
"The workers told me he had dropped the weapon inside the shop before leaving.
"However, he was still waving what appeared to be the sword's sheath as he walked away," she said.
Yani believed the suspect targeted the jewellery shop because security was inadequate.
"There was no security guard on duty at the shop. Perhaps that was why he chose this particular outlet.
"I also believe he deliberately chose to strike during Friday prayers because there would be fewer people around at that time," she said.
Meanwhile, supermarket employee Lim, 51, said he saw the suspect leaving while he was collecting shopping trolleys.
He said the man was fully covered and wore a face mask and helmet, making it difficult to identify him.
"I saw the man leave, but I could not see his face because it was completely covered.
"I could not intervene because I recently suffered a stroke. I was also worried that he might harm me," he said.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said investigators had recorded statements from employees of the jewellery shop and several other witnesses to assist in the investigation.
"Efforts are also underway to analyse closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage to determine the
suspect's escape route
after leaving the premises," he said.
Police are continuing efforts to track down the suspect.
It was reported that the suspect fled with over RM300,000 in jewellery.
"An investigation paper has been opened under Sections 392 and 397 of the Penal Code, while efforts are underway to track down the suspect," he said.
Those with information can contact the nearest police station or the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters at 03-7966 2222.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar says technology must go hand in hand with good values
Article:
KOTA BARU: Parents must instil good values and moral character in their children as the country advances in technology and artificial intelligence.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he would continue educating and reminding parents of their responsibility, stressing that national development must also be rooted in religious values, good manners and moral principles.
Anwar is in Kelantan for a one-day visit centred on meeting the people.
Speaking at the launch of the Skim Usahawan Bangkit Negeri Kelantan, Anwar said the issue was close to his heart and should not be viewed through a political lens.
"This is not about politics. It requires awareness and commitment from everyone.
"I am not trying to shirk my responsibilities as a member of the government. I will continue to do my best," he said.
Anwar said that while much attention was being given to entrepreneurship and economic development, equal emphasis must be placed on nurturing good character and moral values among the younger generation.
He stressed that parents played a crucial role in giving their children a strong foundation in life, particularly through religious education and good upbringing.
"We keep talking about entrepreneurs, but we must also talk about religion, manners and moral values.
"I will continue explaining this every day. Today, I am in Kelantan, and tomorrow I will be in another state.
"I will never grow tired of reminding parents about the basic things they must teach their children, including reading the Quran, practising good manners and developing strong moral values," he said.
Also present was Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah MMA seeks urgent deployment of doctors
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) has called on the Health Ministry to deploy more doctors from Peninsular Malaysia to critically understaffed healthcare facilities across Sabah.
Sabah MMA chairman Dr Brandon Patrick Senagang said reports by CodeBlue highlighted the severe workload and inadequate rest faced by doctors in Ranau, some of whom had worked between 48 and 72 consecutive hours.
"Their dedication deserves recognition, but it must be matched with practical support and timely relief. We cannot allow extraordinary personal sacrifice to become the routine basis on which essential healthcare services operate," he said in a statement.
He said 11 of Hospital Ranau's 19 medical officers had been transferred out following the recent permanent appointment exercise.
Of the seven designated replacements from outside Sabah, only one had reported for duty, leaving the hospital operating with nine doctors, including its director.
The Sabah State Health Department also reported an estimated statewide shortfall of 245 medical officers following the exercise, with 67 per cent of replacement candidates from outside Sabah failing to report for duty.
Brandon said the state health department's efforts to deploy three additional medical officers to Ranau in stages were constrained by similar shortages at other facilities across Sabah.
MMA Sabah called for an immediate, coordinated deployment programme from Peninsular Malaysia, with clear rotation periods, funded travel and accommodation, and adequate operational support.
"An immediate staffing response must run alongside the permanent recruitment exercise," he said.
The association welcomed a special recruitment exercise to fill 750 permanent medical officer vacancies across Sabah and Sarawak, but said the proposed reporting date of Feb 15, 2027, was too far away to address immediate shortages.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NSTP attracts visitors with subscription promotions, exclusive merchandise
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The New Straits Times Press (NSTP) attracted visitors with print and e-paper subscription promotions at the Cardiac Vascular Sentral Kuala Lumpur (CVSKL) Foundation's Health Screening Programme for Journalists here today.
Visitors were also offered exclusive merchandise as part of the promotions.
The promotional booth was set up in conjunction with the Malaysian Media Council's (MMC) second annual general meeting (AGM).
Visitors were introduced to NSTP's publications and subscription packages, including a complimentary one-year e-paper subscription promotion.
The booth also featured New Straits Times-branded merchandise, including T-shirts, tote bags and umbrellas, as part of efforts to engage readers and promote the company's publications.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil visited the booth and was welcomed by Media Prima News and Current Affairs deputy group managing editor Datuk Farrah Naz Abd Karim, who is also New Straits Times group editor.
NSTP branding and intellectual property executive Muhammad Hazeeq Abdul Wahid said the booth had received encouraging interest from visitors keen to learn more about the company's print and digital offerings.
"We have welcomed many visitors to our booth, and it is encouraging to see their interest in our print and digital publications.
"Many are excited to learn about the complimentary one-year e-paper subscription and the convenience of accessing news digitally.
"We are also introducing visitors to our NST merchandise, including T-shirts, tote bags and umbrellas, as part of our efforts to engage more closely with readers," he said.
Hazeeq said the promotional activities provided an opportunity for NSTP to connect with existing subscribers while introducing its publications to potential new readers.
He said the booth also allowed visitors to learn more about the benefits of digital subscriptions, particularly the convenience of accessing news through electronic editions.
The initiative reflects NSTP's continued efforts to strengthen reader engagement and promote its print and digital platforms.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teen held for throwing stone at KTMB train
Article:
ARAU: A 14-year-old boy was detained after throwing a stone at a Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) train, shattering a carriage window and injuring a passenger.
The incident occurred on Thursday at 5.58pm as the
train was travelling
from Arau to Kodiang.
Arau police chief Superintendent Ahmad Mohsin Md Rodi said the teenager was detained at a house in Kampung Guar Sanji today.
"The boy admitted deliberately throwing a stone at the train window.
"He was with four friends near the Kampung Jelempok motorcycle overpass at the time," he said in a statement.
Mohsin said the four friends witnessed the incident but were not involved.
A window on the left side of the middle carriage was shattered.
A female passenger sustained minor injuries to her hand, while the train was delayed by 23 minutes.
Police seized a mobile phone, a SIM card and a stone to assist investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 427 of the Penal Code for mischief, which carries a penalty of between one and five years' imprisonment, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ramanan, Fadhlina confident economic strength, political stability will give PH an edge
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Pakatan Harapan (PH) is confident that the country's improving economic conditions and current political stability could give the coalition an advantage in the 16th Melaka state election on Nov 14.
PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the Madani government's achievements over nearly four years in power, including the strengthening of the ringgit and inflow of foreign investments, must be effectively communicated to the people throughout the campaign period.
Speaking to the media at the Machap Jaya Nomination Centre at the JAPERUN Machap Jaya Complex in Bukit Bulat today, he said the election outcome remained open and would depend on the people's acceptance of the respective coalitions' proposals and efforts.
Ramanan, who is also human resources minister, said PH candidates needed to meet voters on the ground and explain the government's achievements, initiatives and plans for implementation in their interests.
"The information we have, our achievements and what we have implemented must reach the people. Otherwise, they will not know what is being done.
"Therefore, the delivery of messages and information to the people at the grassroots level needs to be improved," he said.
Meanwhile, PKR Wanita chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said PH's candidate for Machap Jaya, Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin of PKR, had extensive political experience and was no stranger to voters in Melaka.
She said Lim's experience, having previously won the seat and served as Melaka's Women, Family Development, Welfare and Orang Asli Affairs executive councillor, gave her an advantage in terms of experience and familiarity among the local community.
Fadhlina said Machap Jaya was among the seats with significant potential for PH to win, although it was expected to face a stiff challenge from incumbent Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem (BN-MCA).
"I think this is an evenly matched contest, as both sides are relying on their respective track records, achievements and administrative service. This is a very good opportunity for PH, given the current situation which offers several advantages, including economic stability and the budget," said Fadhlina, who is also education minister.
She also commended PKR's decision to field three women candidates in this Melaka state election.
Earlier, Ramanan and Fadhlina, together with PKR vice-president performing the duties of deputy president and PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, who is also home minister, and PKR Central Leadership Council member Dr Maszlee Malik, accompanied Lim to the Machap Jaya nomination centre.
The Machap Jaya State seat will see a three-cornered contest involving Lim, Ngwe and B. Prasanth Kumar, who is representing Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, while early voting will be held on Nov 10.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Employee transfers RM486,000 company money, deceived by individual impersonating employer
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A woman fell victim to a scam after being deceived by a person who impersonated her employer, resulting in the transfer of RM486,000 from the company.
Acting Johor Baru Utara district police chief superintendent Azrol Anuar Nor said the 35-year-old victim was deceived through a short message service (SMS) from the individual who impersonated her company manager in the incident at 10am.
He said the victim was instructed to transfer the company's money to the suspect's account under the pretext of payment of a new contract.
Azrol Anuar said the victim, however, realised she was being scammed after being asked to make an additional transaction of the same amount under a different pretext.
"The victim also failed to contact the real employer through a WhatsApp call before discovering that the employer's phone number had been hacked," he said in a statement.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
The public is advised to always be vigilant against any money transfer instructions and to check through the SemakMule portal or contact the NSRC 997 line if they fall victims to scams.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AGC reviewing candidate selection for proposed separation of top legal roles
Article:
KOTA BARU: The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) is reviewing provisions on the selection of candidates under a proposal to separate the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said this followed the tabling of the Bill on the proposed separation.
"The Bill on the proposed separation of the roles of attorney-general and public prosecutor has been tabled and has gone through the proper process, including consideration by the Parliamentary Special Select Committee (PSSC).
"On the issue of candidates, we are reviewing a provision concerning how they should be selected," he said.
He was speaking at the opening and handover of recreational facilities under the Attorney-General's Chambers' Kampung Angkat Madani programme in Kampung Kok Lanas yesterday.
Reports previously stated the PSSC would resume its meeting after receiving feedback from the A-GC on the proposed separation of the roles.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the A-GC had been given two weeks to provide a detailed response.
On Mar 3, the Constitution (Amendment) Bill (No. 2) 2026, which seeks to separate the roles of attorney-general and public prosecutor, was referred to the PSSC.
Under the proposed framework, the public prosecutor would oversee all criminal prosecutions, while the attorney-general would serve as the government's legal adviser on matters other than criminal law.
The public prosecutor would be appointed by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong at His Majesty's discretion, on the advice of the Judicial and Legal Service Commission, after consulting the Conference of Rulers.
The proposal differs from the current arrangement, under which the
attorney-general is appointed
by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on the advice of the Prime Minister.
Meanwhile, Dusuki said RM500,000 had been allocated to upgrade public facilities and improve residents' well-being under the Attorney-General's Chambers' Kampung Angkat Madani programme in Kampung Kok Lanas.
He said the infrastructure improvements covered not only physical facilities but also supported healthy lifestyles, small-scale economic activities and the well-being of the local community.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi offers condolences to family of Mata Ayer state assemblyman Wan Badariah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has expressed his condolences to the family of Mata Ayer State Assemblyman Wan Badariah Wan Saad, who passed away today.
“My deepest condolences to the entire family of the deceased, as well as to her friends and fellow comrades,” he said in a Facebook post.
Fahmi also prayed that Allah SWT would forgive the deceased’s sins, bless her soul, and place her among the believers and the righteous.
Wan Badariah passed away at Tuanku Fauziah Hospital in Kangar at 4.26pm.
The deceased won the Mata Ayer seat under the Perikatan Nasional ticket during the 15th General Election with a majority of 2,021 votes. — Bernama

Title: Anwar directs Education Ministry to act firmly on school bullying
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Ministry of Education (MOE) to take firm action against bullying in schools amid growing concerns over children’s safety and well-being.
He said cases involving children, including suicide, abuse and bullying, highlighted the need to strengthen character development and moral values from an early age.
Anwar said academic excellence alone was insufficient, stressing that education must also instil good manners, respect and a sense of responsibility among students.
“Bullying and humiliating others show that there are still shortcomings in instilling values and proper conduct in our education system.
“The Education Ministry has been directed to be firm and take decisive action. Teachers and educators must also help look after our children,” he said at the launch of the Kelantan Entrepreneur Revival Scheme here today.
Anwar also stressed the importance of religious education, including understanding and practising the teachings of the Quran, performing prayers and respecting parents, teachers and peers.
He said addressing social problems such as drug abuse and crime required a comprehensive approach to ensure young people grew up in a healthy environment. — Bernama

Title: Anwar, Lawrence Wong to witness JS-SEZ master plan launch; Perak venue under review, says Akmal Nasrullah
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 31 — The government is considering Perak as the venue for the launch of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) master plan, which could coincide with the two countries’ Annual Leaders’ Retreat scheduled to be held in the state on December 4.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said it had been agreed that the launch would be witnessed jointly by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Singaporean counterpart, Lawrence Wong.
“Both prime ministers have agreed to witness the launch of the master plan. We are now finalising the venue, as this year’s Annual Leaders’ Retreat is expected to be held in Ipoh.
“We are considering whether the launch will take place there or whether other arrangements will be made. However, both prime ministers have agreed to witness the ceremony,” he told a press conference after the Johor Bahru parliamentary constituency’s Deepavali celebration in Larkin here today.
On preparations for Monday’s bilateral meeting in Singapore, Akmal Nasrullah said Singapore would host the meeting.
He described the meeting as significant as it would be the first to be held under the Johor-Singapore Cooperation Ministerial Committee framework.
He is scheduled to lead the Malaysian delegation alongside Johor Menteri Besar Onn Hafiz Ghazi, while Singapore’s delegation will be led by National Development Minister Chee Hong Tat.
“From Malaysia’s perspective, this meeting presents an opportunity to assess progress in implementing the JS-SEZ initiative and discuss plans for the way forward,” he said.
Akmal Nasrullah said the programme framework and logistical arrangements for the Annual Leaders’ Retreat were being refined to maximise its impact following the launch of the master plan.
On the Deepavali celebration, he said a total of RM318,000 had been allocated to improve community well-being in the Johor Bahru parliamentary constituency.
He presented RM260,000 under the Prime Minister’s Office’s Madani Infrastructure and Social Response Programme (PRISMA) for repairs to staircase handrails at Rumah Pangsa Serantau Baru in Larkin.
He said the infrastructure improvements were aimed at enhancing residents’ safety and comfort, particularly for senior citizens, children and other vulnerable groups.
A further RM47,500 was allocated to upgrade places of worship serving the Indian community, while RM10,500 was distributed among four local non-governmental organisations to support welfare, cultural and community development programmes. — Bernama

Title: National Courier Day: Govt pledges reform as RM6.9b courier sector takes spotlight
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 31 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today launched the National Courier Day 2026 (HKN2026) celebration, recognising the industry’s RM6.9 billion contribution to the country’s digital economy, at the Selangor International Trade Centre.
Themed “Sustaining the Industry, Strengthening Trust,” the event was organised by the Malaysian Express Carriers Association (AMEC) with support from the Communications Ministry through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
MCMC said the government remains committed to strengthening the postal and courier industry through regulatory reform, strategic cooperation and digital transformation to improve service efficiency, industry competitiveness and consumer safety.
“On regulatory reform, the government is reviewing proposed amendments to the Postal Services Act 2012 (Act 741) and plans to gazette the Postal Services Regulations (Postal Service Security and Prohibited Postal Articles) 2026 (PSR2026), subject to the relevant approval process.
“These measures aim to strengthen security, industry accountability and consumer protection, in step with the rapid growth of e-commerce,” MCMC said in a statement today.
Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah, MCMC managing director Abdul Karim Fakir Ali, AMEC chairman Ronald Tan, and representatives of government agencies, postal and courier industry players.
Parcel Shield, an initiative led by the Postal Forum with MCMC support, was also launched at HKN2026 to tackle parcel delivery fraud.
“The initiative, among others, encourages information sharing between courier companies and e-commerce platforms, and the dissemination of fraud alerts to enhance consumer protection and confidence,” the statement read.
HKN2026 further saw the signing of a memorandum of collaboration for the Courier Network Sharing initiative, a last-mile delivery pilot at selected locations.
“The project will assess the potential for infrastructure optimisation, reduced operational overlap and improved service access before expansion is considered,” the statement read.
Additionally, digital transformation is being strengthened through the National Address System (NAS) to improve address accuracy and delivery efficiency, and PAKEJ Map, which helps users locate more than 47,000 postal and courier service points nationwide.
HKN2026 further recognised industry personnel through the Best Courier Worker award, the Safe Driving Challenge and the MyCSP Courier Safety Passport programme, with emphasis on safety and service quality. — Bernama

Title: Nga Kor Ming urges global cooperation on housing crisis, cites 3.4 billion affected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Stronger international cooperation is needed to address the global housing crisis, with approximately 3.4 billion people worldwide experiencing some form of inadequate housing, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming.
In making the call, Nga, who is also United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) Assembly president, said that more than 1.16 billion people lived in informal settlements, including slums, while 44 per cent of urban renters spent an unsustainable proportion of their income on rent.
“Governments must ensure that housing is affordable, safe, well-connected to public transport and employment opportunities, and supported by essential public amenities,” he said in his keynote address at the opening ceremony of the Global Observance of World Cities Day 2026 in Fuzhou, China, today.
The event, themed “Regenerating the City: Adequate Housing for All”, is jointly organised by UN-Habitat, China’s Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, the Fujian Provincial People’s Government and the Fuzhou Municipal People’s Government.
Nga said addressing the crisis required more than building additional homes, as rising housing costs placed increasing pressure on households and widened social inequalities.
He urged governments, international organisations, and the private sector to strengthen partnerships in affordable housing, green development and sustainable urban regeneration.
Sharing Malaysia’s experience, Nga said the government had set a target of delivering one million affordable homes between 2026 and 2035, alongside an ambition to place Malaysia among the world’s top 10 countries for home ownership by 2035.
He highlighted the Malaysia Madani vision, the country’s housing reform agenda, and the National Housing Policy 2026-2035 as key initiatives to improve housing accessibility and support sustainable urban development.
Nga also cited the RM60 billion Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP), which facilitates access to home financing for 150,000 individuals without conventional income documentation.
“Housing is the foundational soil from which all human capability grows. It is where our children form their earliest ambitions, where working parents recharge their spirit, and where our senior citizens enjoy the honour they have earned over a lifetime.
“When a household enjoys a secure roof, every aspect of life stabilises. Health improves, educational outcomes soar, and economic confidence takes root,” he said.
Nga said a city’s success should be measured by the liveability of its neighbourhoods, the quality of public spaces, environmental protection and opportunities for residents, rather than merely its skyline or the scale of construction.
He said housing must cater to people’s needs from early childhood through to elderly care, while urban regeneration should support climate action through energy-efficient technologies and expanded green spaces.
Malaysia was also promoting transit-oriented development and climate-resilient urban renewal as part of its efforts to build more sustainable communities, he also said.
“Policy without execution is merely good intention, vision without action is only a dream,” he added, urging world leaders to translate international commitments into tangible improvements in people’s lives. — Bernama

Title: KL police arrest 18 Taiwanese for posing as Hong Kong police in online scam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Police detained 18 Taiwanese nationals suspected of involvement in an online scam syndicate impersonating Hong Kong police after raids on two luxury apartment units here on Thursday.
Dang Wangi police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said 17 men and one woman, aged between 19 and 43, were arrested during the 6.35pm raid.
“Police seized 69 mobile phones, five laptops, and two sets of Hong Kong police uniforms,” he said in a statement today.
He added that based on the items recovered, the syndicate is suspected of cheating by posing as Hong Kong police officers and targeting victims in the special administrative region of China.
Ahmad Azwan said initial investigations found the syndicate used local internet access and has likely been operating for about five months.
All suspects have been remanded for four days until November 2 to assist in the investigation under Section 420/511 of the Penal Code.
He also urged members of the public with information about such activities to contact the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters at 03-26002222 or any nearby police station. — Bernama

Title: Anwar contributes RM200,000 to madrasah in Pondok Lubuk Tapah for repairs
Article:
PASIR MAS, Oct 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today presented a contribution of RM200,000 to Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah Pondok Lubuk Tapah here.
The mock cheque, presented under the Kelantan Islamic Educational Institutions Maintenance and Repair Project 2026, was handed over to the madrasah’s chairman, Assoc Prof Datuk Dr Luqman Abdullah.
During the programme, Anwar also spent about 30 minutes visiting Luqman’s residence before performing Maghrib prayers with over 100 local residents.
Also present were Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud and Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat.
Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah Pondok Lubuk Tapah was founded in 1931. — Bernama
