Title: RM16b in SARA, STR aid for Malaysians as helping the poor won’t bankrupt the govt, says Anwar
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — The government will not become poor or go bankrupt by helping the less fortunate, as the real threats to the country’s economy are misconduct among leaders, corruption and financial leakages, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said providing assistance to low-income groups was the government’s responsibility to ensure that the benefits of national development were shared more widely among the people.
Anwar cited the government’s allocation of RM16 billion this year for the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) and Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) assistance programmes, alongside increases in civil servants’ salaries and the minimum wage, as measures aimed at improving the people’s well-being.
“No country or government has ever become poor simply by helping the poor,” he said when launching the Kelantan Entrepreneur Revival Scheme here today.
He said a country’s economy could suffer if public wealth was exploited to serve the interests of certain groups, particularly through corruption and greed in the administration.
The Prime Minister stressed that the government must continue to uphold its commitment to helping those in need while maintaining sound financial management and good governance. — Bernama

Title: Anwar unveils additional RM200m grant to support low-income, small-scale entrepreneurs
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — The government has allocated an additional grant of about RM200 million to strengthen the capacity of small-scale entrepreneurs, particularly those from low-income groups, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said small-scale financial assistance could generate meaningful returns for traders if channelled to meet their specific business requirements.
He gave the example of traders who required between RM1,800 and RM5,000 to acquire basic equipment, including refrigerators, to preserve their stock.
“Although the allocation is modest, the benefits go directly to those who need it,” he said when officiating the Kelantan Usahawan Bangkit Scheme here today.
Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud was also present.
Anwar said the federal government was stepping up support for women in Kelantan through entrepreneurship initiatives, recognizing their significant role in the state’s small business sector, including among B40 assistance recipients, and giving them greater opportunities to expand their businesses.
He said women in Kelantan had a strong track record and extensive experience in business, particularly through selling goods at markets, which demonstrated their determination to earn a living.
“That is why I have instructed the Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU) in Kelantan to prioritise assistance programmes for women,” he said.
The Prime Minister said women’s business acumen was evident in Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia’s nearly 99 per cent loan repayment rate.
On the Kelantan Usahawan Bangkit Scheme, Anwar said more than 4,000 applications had been received from B40 entrepreneurs, with 446 approved so far.
“The scheme provides financial support to small-scale entrepreneurs looking to expand their businesses. So far, more than 4,000 applications have been received from B40 entrepreneurs under Sejati Madani, with 446 approved,” he said.
In another development, the Prime Minister renewed his call for Malaysia to enhance its mastery of emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), digital technology and quantum technology, while upholding religious values, culture and national identity.
He highlighted the importance of keeping pace with global technological developments to ensure the younger generation remained competitive with those in developed nations.
He said the national education system should therefore expand the use of the latest knowledge and technologies, including by introducing the fundamentals of AI at an early stage of schooling.
According to him, national development should be guided by the concept of reaching for the skies while remaining rooted in the earth, which means pursuing advances in knowledge and technology while preserving society’s values and identity.
“This country must progress and master new technologies, including information technology and artificial intelligence, but it must also remain rooted in traditions, a culture grounded in faith, good morals and strong character,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Golok River mouth widening project to cut flood risk, talks with Thailand to wrap up within a month
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — Malaysia and Thailand are expected to finalise negotiations on the Golok River mouth widening project within a month to reduce flood risks in Kelantan and southern Thailand.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he had held two rounds of talks with the Thai government, including with his counterpart Anutin Charnvirakul, to expedite the implementation of the project.
He said widening and deepening the river mouth was among the key measures to mitigate the impact of floods affecting areas in both countries.
“I hope to resume negotiations within this month to finalise the matter. There has already been progress between the Malaysian and Thai governments,” he said when speaking at the Kelantan State Entrepreneur Revival Scheme Launch Ceremony here today.
Also present was Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.
The Prime Minister said close cooperation between the two countries was important to ensure the issue could be resolved effectively, thereby benefiting residents in Kelantan and southern Thailand.
He said good relations with neighbouring countries were important not only in terms of trade, but also in addressing cross-border issues that required joint solutions.
On the flood situation in Kelantan, Anwar gave an assurance that the Federal Government would continue to assist the state in implementing flood mitigation projects, despite the substantial allocations required due to high construction costs.
He said the matter had been discussed with the Kelantan Menteri Besar to facilitate an integrated approach through close cooperation between the state and Federal governments, thereby reducing the impact of floods on the people and the state’s development.
In this regard, Anwar said the government planned to develop the area around the Rantau Panjang Bridge to give the locality a new look through development projects planned in collaboration with the state government.
The Prime Minister stressed that the success of the initiative required firm commitment from both sides, particularly in expediting land acquisition matters.
In this regard, he expressed his appreciation to Kelantan State Secretary Datuk Dr Tengku Mohamed Faziharudean Tengku Feissal for helping to expedite the necessary processes to facilitate the implementation of the development project.
“We are also taking this opportunity to develop the area around the Rantau Panjang Bridge. My thanks to the State Secretary for expediting land acquisition and other related matters so that we can proceed with the project, with the hope of giving Rantau Panjang a new look and bringing progress to the area,” he said.
Anwar said the development was among the government’s efforts to drive socioeconomic growth in the border area, in addition to addressing issues related to the mouth of the Golok River. — Bernama

Title: All relief centres closed in Kedah, Negeri Sembilan as floods subside, Perak evacuees fall to 25
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Floods in Kedah and Negeri Sembilan have fully subsided, with all three temporary relief centres (PPS) in the two states closed today, while the number of evacuees in Perak has declined.
In Kedah, the last relief centre in Pendang, Dewan Pejabat Penghulu Mukim Bukit Raya, which had been open since last Wednesday, was closed at 10am, allowing all nine evacuees from two families to return home after the floodwaters receded completely.
In Negeri Sembilan, two relief centres in Kuala Pilah, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Undang Johol and Dewan Orang Ramai Dangi, which housed 87 evacuees from 35 families, were also closed at 4pm today following improved weather and the complete recession of floodwaters.
In Perak, the flood situation has also improved, with the number of evacuees at SK Titi Serong relief centre in Kerian declining to 25 from nine families, compared with 34 people from 12 families this morning.
The Perak State Disaster Management Committee secretariat said in a statement that all evacuees from Taman Aman Sejahtera and Taman Desa Aman 1 had been housed at the centre since Thursday.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecast rain tonight in Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim. — Bernama

Title: No unhealthy readings: Cheras highest at 77 as 47 areas nationwide record moderate API readings this afternoon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — A total of 47 areas across the country recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at a moderate level as of this evening, while 21 areas recorded good air quality.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollution Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Cheras here recorded the highest moderate API reading at 77, followed by Batu Muda (72). In Selangor, the affected areas include Johan Setia (76), Klang (74), Shah Alam (64), Banting (62), Petaling Jaya (60), and Kuala Selangor (55).
In Johor, the areas are Larkin (73), Kluang (67), Tangkak (62), Pasir Gudang (61), Segamat (56), as well as Pengerang and Kota Tinggi (53 each).
Negeri Sembilan recorded moderate readings in Nilai (69), Seremban (63), and Port Dickson (57), while in Perak, the areas involved are Tasek Ipoh (66), Seri Manjung (56), Pegoh in Ipoh (55), and Taiping (54).
Putrajaya recorded a reading of 65, while in Penang, the areas are Seberang Perai (64), Seberang Jaya (55), and Minden (52).
In Sarawak, seven areas recorded moderate readings: Mukah (64), IPD Serian (59), Kuching (57), Samalaju (56), Sri Aman (55), Sibu (53), and Samarahan (51).
Melaka recorded readings in Bandaraya Melaka (63), Bukit Rambai (62), and Alor Gajah (61), while in Pahang, the area involved is Balok Baru in Kuantan (61).
In Sabah, the areas are Tawau (61), Keningau (55), Kimanis (54), and Sandakan (52), while in Kelantan, they involve Kota Bharu (59) and Tanah Merah (52).
Kedah also recorded moderate readings in Sungai Petani (58) and Kulim Hi-Tech (51), while Kuala Terengganu in Terengganu recorded a reading of 55, and Labuan recorded 52.
Meanwhile, a total of 21 areas recorded good API readings as of this evening, compared to 24 areas in the morning.
API readings between 0 and 50 are categorized as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and 301 and above as hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Perlis PAS announces death of Mata Ayer rep Wan Badariah
Article:
KANGAR, Oct 31 — Mata Ayer assemblywoman Wan Badariah Wan Saad died at Hospital Tuanku Fauziah (HTF) here at 4.26pm today.
Perlis PAS Information chief Mohamad Zahid Ibrahim announced her death in a post on the Perlis PAS Facebook page.
He also extended condolences to her family and urged the public to pray for her soul.
“May Allah shower His blessings upon her soul, forgive her sins and place her among the faithful and the righteous.
“My condolences to all members of her family,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Baby buried in Kapit still hospitalised; mother’s postpartum depression link unconfirmed, says Nancy Shukri
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 31 — The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) has yet to receive medical confirmation on whether the mother of a baby boy found buried in Kapit recently was suffering from postpartum depression.
Its Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said registered counsellors and hospital medical personnel had important roles to play in identifying the underlying issues faced by the mother.
“We do not know yet, which is why counsellors play a very important role. The Health Ministry also needs to involve the doctors and nurses handling the case.
“I cannot comment beyond what we know so far, as the police are still investigating the case, but our protection team is working with the family and counsellors to determine the actual problem so that they can provide assistance,” she told a press conference after officiating the KPWKM Santuni Kasih Programme here today.
Nancy said discussions on whether the baby would be placed under the care of family members or other suitable parties had yet to be concluded, as both the mother and baby were understood to still be receiving hospital treatment.
She also advised mothers in need of emotional and postnatal health support to seek assistance through the MamaCare initiative, managed by the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN).
Earlier, Kapit police chief DSP Rohana Nanu was reported as saying that a baby boy who was still alive was found buried in the ground near a rented house in Jalan Airport, Kapit, on Wednesday.
The baby, who was initially reported to be in critical condition, was rushed to Sibu Hospital for specialist treatment, while the case is being investigated under Section 317 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Not compulsory, but journalists, your annual check-up could soon come with your press card
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 31 — The Malaysian Media Council (MMC) should explore mechanisms to encourage media practitioners to undergo health screenings during the process of issuing media passes.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the proposed initiative is crucial to ensure that as many as possible of the 12,000 personnel in the media sector benefit and have health issues identified at an early stage.
“I do not want to say to make it compulsory, but we must encourage them. Perhaps the Information Department, before issuing the annual media accreditation card, could ask if they have undergone a medical check-up,” he said today.
He said this in his speech at the launch of the Journalists’ Health Screening Programme with the Cardiac Vascular Sentral Kuala Lumpur (CVSKL) Foundation ahead of the 2026 MMC Annual General Meeting here.
Also present were Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) Chief Executive Officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, CVSKL Foundation chairman Tan Sri Rashpal Singh, ECM Libra Foundation chairman Datuk Seri Kalimullah Masheerul Hassan and MMC chairman Tan Sri Nallini Pathmanathan.
Fahmi later told reporters that the proposal for media practitioners to undergo annual health screening has not been set as a prerequisite for media card holders, adding that it would be discussed with the MMC in detail first.
“We will discuss this with the Media Council (and) with all media companies to assess its feasibility; for instance, if this initiative involves facilities in the Klang Valley, it may pose some difficulties for our colleagues in Sabah and Sarawak, or in areas outside the Klang Valley.
“We do not intend to make it compulsory, but we would like to encourage all media teams to undergo health screenings at least once a year. That is our intention,” he said.
On today’s programme, he said the RM1 million initiative, contributed by ECM Libra Foundation to the CVSKL Foundation, aimed to help improve access to preventive healthcare services, particularly for active and former journalists.
“We view problems involving the health of journalists as one of the key issues. These screenings can help identify non-communicable diseases at an early stage, allowing us to provide assistance earlier and help prevent any untoward incidents from occurring,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Puchong chicken supplier shut for two weeks after halal breach discovery, restaurants told to stop buying from it
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 31 — A premises in Puchong, suspected of slaughtering, processing and distributing chicken without valid halal certification, was found to be using the electric water-bath stunning method.
Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said preliminary inspections found that the electrical voltage used was believed to be too high, causing the chickens to die instantly before undergoing slaughter in accordance with Islamic law.
“Early this morning, the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais), in collaboration with the police, the Selangor Department of Environment (DOE), the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) and the Petaling District Health Office, led a raid on premises allegedly involved in slaughtering chickens in a manner that did not comply with Islamic requirements.
“Preliminary investigations found that the premises used the stunning method, whereby the chickens were found dead before being slaughtered. This means they were essentially slaughtering carcasses rather than live chickens, as required under Islamic teachings,” he told reporters.
He said this after attending the 2026 Selangor-level Ahli Sunnah Wal Jamaah (ASWJ) Fundamental Declaration Programme, which was also attended by Jais director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad, at the Dewan Syarahan dan Muzakarah Islam, Masjid Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah, here today.
He added that the situation had raised serious doubts over compliance with Islamic law, and the halal status of the processed chicken products, making this a key focus of the authorities’ investigation to determine the actual operating methods used.
Elaborating, Salehuddin said preliminary investigations also found that the slaughterhouse had been operating since 2004, and was believed to be owned by a Muslim, besides supplying processed chicken to restaurants also owned by Muslims.
“If it is true that this is a Muslim-owned factory which had killed the chickens before slaughtering them, this is a highly irresponsible act, and we will ensure that firm action is taken.
“The company has been operating for a long time, for more than 20 years. I am therefore rather perplexed as to how something like this could happen, and why they would so easily deceive Muslims when they themselves are Muslims.
Salehuddin said the issue was also linked to the absence of mandatory halal certification requirements for certain premises. However, operators should be aware that the meat supply in question was prohibited under Islamic law.
Following the raid, he said that the authorities had ordered the factory premises to be closed for two weeks under health regulations, to allow for a detailed assessment and investigation.
In this regard, Salehuddin urged restaurant owners receiving supplies from the company to stop using them immediately, and report any suspicious information to Jais, Jakim or the police.
“I urge Muslims, restaurant operators and food business owners to check the source of their chicken supplies, in particular, as they must ensure that the food they serve is suitable for consumption by Muslims.
“Earlier, Jais seized more than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken, worth RM85,400, after finding that the poultry had been processed without complying with Islamic slaughtering requirements. The seizure was made during a raid at a warehouse in Puchong at 12.40 am today, under Op Taring Chiller.
Earlier, the 2026 Selangor-level ASWJ Fundamental Declaration programme brought together nearly 500 participants, including teachers, mosque administrators, marriage registrars, local authorities (PBT) and religious agencies, to deepen their understanding of the importance of safeguarding the faith, through presentations of two working papers. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Mais stands for Majlis Agama Islam Selangor, Jais stands for Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor, and Jakim stands for Jabatan Kemajuan Islam Malaysia. PBT stands for Pihak Berkuasa Tempatan, and Op stands for Operasi. ASWJ stands for Ahli Sunnah Wal Jamaah, an Arabic term for mainstream Sunni Islam.

Title: ‘Boss’ texts, RM486,000 gone: Johor Bahru woman duped by fake employer
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 31 — A woman fell victim to a scam after being deceived by an individual who impersonated her employer, resulting in the transfer of RM486,000 from the company.
Acting Johor Bahru Utara district police chief Supt Azrol Anuar Nor said the 35-year-old victim was deceived through a short message service (SMS) from the individual who impersonated her company manager in the incident at 10 am.
He said the victim was instructed to transfer the company’s money to the suspect’s account under the pretext of payment of a new contract.
Azrol Anuar said the victim, however, realised she was being scammed after being asked to make an additional transaction of the same amount under a different pretext.
“The victim also failed to contact the real employer through a WhatsApp call before discovering that the employer’s phone number had been hacked,” he said in a statement.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
The public is advised to always be vigilant against any money transfer instructions and to check through the SemakMule portal or contact the NSRC 997 line if they fall victims to scams. — Bernama
Editor’s note: Supt stands for Superintendent. SMS stands for Short Message Service. NSRC stands for National Scam Response Centre.

Title: Amanah vs Umno in Merlimau: Rahayu knows Dr Akmal is big on social media, so she’s counting on voters at the grassroots
Article:
JASIN, Oct 31 — A father’s advice to always remain strong and broad-minded has inspired Melaka Amanah Wanita chief Rahayu Hamzah to take on the challenge of contesting the Merlimau state seat for Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the 16th Melaka state election.
She said the advice had become her guiding principle, particularly as she prepares to face Barisan Nasional (BN) incumbent Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh.
Acknowledging Dr Muhamad Akmal’s strong social media influence as Umno Youth chief, Rahayu said she remained confident of PH’s support among voters in the constituency.
“We recognise his social media influence, but we are prepared. I believe in the support of voters on the ground, and that is why I am ready to take on this challenge,” she told reporters here today.
Rahayu said that if elected, she would focus on serving the community in line with PH’s Melaka Rumah Kita aspirations, with education for young people among her priorities.
She also pledged to address local infrastructure concerns, including flooding, based on residents’ needs and complaints.
Meanwhile, Dr Muhamad Akmal said he was not targeting a large majority in Merlimau but instead sought voters’ confidence based on his service over the past four years and 11 months.
“If they feel my service has not been good, I honestly say they should not vote for me. But if they are satisfied with my performance, I ask for their trust once again,” he said.
Dr Muhamad Akmal said he was prepared to face criticism and allegations from his opponents during the campaign, adding that voters were capable of assessing the information presented to them.
He also urged all campaign teams to conduct their activities maturely and responsibly, and to refrain from provocation, slander and remarks intended to discredit others.
The Merlimau seat will see a straight fight between Dr Muhamad Akmal and Rahayu.
Polling day is set for November 14, while early voting will take place on November 10.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: No five- or six-cornered fights in 28 seats: Melaka’s 2026 ballot looks very different from 2021
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — The 16th Melaka State Election features 11 straight fights and 11 three-cornered contests across the 28 state constituencies, following the conclusion of the nomination process today.
The remaining six constituencies will see four-cornered contests, marking a significant shift from the 2021 state election, which was dominated by five- and six-cornered races, with no straight fights.
Among the straight fights attracting attention is Tanjung Bidara, where incumbent Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh of Barisan Nasional (BN) faces Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri, who is making his electoral debut.
In Rim, incumbent Datuk Khaidhirah Abu Zahar, better known as Dira, will face PH candidate Esma Eazreen Husin, the Jasin division chief of the Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Women’s Wing.
Duyong will see a straight fight between incumbent Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem of BN and PH candidate Poo Long Suan, a member of the DAP Melaka Complaints Committee. In Merlimau, incumbent Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh of BN will be challenged by PH candidate Rahayu Hamzah.
Among the three-cornered contests, Machap Jaya will see incumbent Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem of BN face former assemblyman Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin of PH and B. Prasanth Kumar of Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
In Paya Rumput, prime minister’s political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin, representing PH, will face Rafie Ahmad of Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar of Bersama.
Bandar Hilir will see incumbent Leng Chau Yen of PH contest against BN candidate Jasmine Lok Huey Yee and Dr Mohd Nor Rashidi Ab Jalil of Bersama.
Meanwhile, Bukit Katil and Ayer Keroh will each see four-cornered contests.
In Bukit Katil, incumbent and Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari will face PN candidate Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif, Bersama candidate Dr Aliza Che Amran and independent candidate Abu Bakar Sabudin.
In Ayer Keroh, incumbent Kerk Chee Yee of PH will be challenged by Datuk Seri Michael Gan Peng Lam of PN, Mohd Hamnaim Mohamad of Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) and Muhammad Muhaimin Lau Abdullah of Bersama.
The 28-seat Melaka State Legislative Assembly was dissolved on September 23 with the consent of Yang Dipertua Negeri of Melaka Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 10 for early voting and November 14 as polling day.
A total of 687,697 voters are eligible to cast their ballots, comprising 675,166 ordinary voters, 9,769 military personnel and their spouses, and 2,762 police personnel.
In the 15th Melaka State Election on November 20, 2021, BN won 21 seats, with UMNO securing 18, MCA two and MIC one, enabling the coalition to form the state government with a more than two-thirds majority.
PH won five seats, with DAP securing four and Amanah one, while PN won two.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Three or four checks, then one big raid: How a Puchong chicken warehouse that flouted halal rules ran for 20 years
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — A chicken slaughtering and processing warehouse in Puchong, raided under Ops Taring Chiller yesterday, is believed to have operated for 20 years.
Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence and Investigation (WCB/PSK) commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said investigations identified the warehouse owner as a 34-year-old local man.
“Check results showed this fresh chicken slaughtering and processing warehouse has operated for roughly 20 years.
“Investigations also revealed that the warehouse owner is a 34-year-old local man, and further investigations into the matter will be continued by the Halal Enforcement Division of the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais),” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
He added that during the warehouse’s operation, Jais and relevant enforcement agencies conducted three to four raids and inspections. Yesterday’s raid was the first involving the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) via WCB/PSK.
Mohd Zaki, in a statement yesterday, confirmed that authorities seized over 6.5 tonnes of chicken suspected to have been processed without adhering to Syariah-compliant slaughtering methods and halal certification requirements during the raid on the warehouse in Puchong.
Also detained in Ops Taring Chiller were 12 Bangladeshi and Pakistani men believed to be involved in slaughtering and processing activities at the premises.
The live chicken supply is believed to have been sourced from several poultry farms around Sepang. The processed chicken was distributed to customers including eateries, grocery stores, and supermarkets across the Klang Valley.
The case is being investigated under Section 3(1)(A) and Section 4(1) of the Trade Descriptions (Definition of Halal) Order 2011, as well as Section 38(1) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: PSK stands for Perisikan dan Siasatan Khas in Malay. Jais stands for Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor, and PDRM stands for Polis Diraja Malaysia.

Title: Too soon to count? PSD hasn’t measured Waze ban compliance yet
Article:
KAMPAR, Oct 31 — The Public Service Department (JPA) is confident that civil servants will fully comply with the ban on the use of the Waze navigation application.
Director-General of Public Service (KPPA) Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said the compliance rate among civil servants had yet to be determined, as the government had only recently announced the directive.
Nevertheless, he expressed confidence that civil servants would take the matter seriously and comply with the ban, which was imposed for security reasons.
“Civil servants are no longer allowed to use Waze due to security concerns. We have also learned from what happened to other countries that used the application,” he said after officiating at the closing ceremony of the Kampung dan Sekolah Angkat Madani JPA programme at Sekolah Kebangsaan Kota Baharu here today.
On October 21, the government decided to ban all civil servants from using the Waze navigation application to protect government information and users’ personal data from the threat of misuse by the Israeli regime.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the decision took into account the fact that Waze Mobile Ltd, which controls user data, is incorporated and operates under Israeli law.
Meanwhile, Wan Ahmad Dahlan said RM1.465 million had been allocated to improve infrastructure, upgrade public facilities and support educational programmes under the Kampung dan Sekolah Angkat Madani programme for residents of Kampung Kota Bharu and students of Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Malim Nawar here.
He said RM500,000 from the Ministry of Finance and an additional RM35,000 from JPA were set aside for eight physical projects under the Kampung Angkat Madani initiative, including upgrades to the mosque, community hall, health clinic, police station and pavilion at SK Kota Baharu, as well as the construction of a village landmark and the provision of smart boards.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan also said collaboration with the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development had resulted in the installation of 40 solar-powered streetlights worth RM380,000, while the Implementation Coordination Unit under the Prime Minister’s Department had allocated RM450,000 for the construction of a new multipurpose hall with two badminton courts.
He said an allocation of RM90,000 was also provided to SMK Malim Nawar to upgrade its computer laboratory, Design and Technology workshop and science laboratories, with another RM10,000 earmarked for educational development programmes for students and teachers.
“Various community and educational activities have also been held, including a korban programme, GP Joran fishing competition, traditional games, health and psychological outreach programme, Tuisyen Madani, gotong-royong activities and Wira Komuniti Carnival,” he said.
The closing ceremony also saw 97 families in Kampung Kota Bharu receive Bakul Rahmah aid, while schools received contributions and JPA’s strategic partners were recognised for their support.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan also praised the SK Kota Baharu team for winning a gold medal for its Ecowire Roll innovation at the International Innovation and Entrepreneurship Expo 2026 on October 25.
He also highlighted the achievement of a female student from SMK Malim Nawar who was selected to represent Selangor in football.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan said these achievements showed that children from rural areas could excel when given the right opportunities, facilities and support. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: JPA stands for Jabatan Perkhidmatan Awam in Malay, also known as PSD in English, while KPPA stands for Ketua Pengarah Perkhidmatan Awam in Malay.

Title: Sabah is short of nearly 245 medical officers, and Ranau Hospital feels it most
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 31 — Sabah is facing a shortage of nearly 245 medical officers following the implementation of the Phase 2 Permanent Appointment exercise on September 28, with Ranau Hospital among the healthcare facilities affected by the transfer of existing medical officers.
The Sabah State Health Department (Sabah JKN) said the shortage was partly due to 67 per cent of replacement candidates from outside Sabah failed to report for duty after accepting offers of permanent appointment, hindering efforts to fill vacancies in the state.
Ranau Hospital is currently operating with only nine medical officers, including the hospital director, after 11 of its 19 medical officers were transferred out under the exercise.
“Although the Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) identified seven replacement officers from outside Sabah, only one has reported for duty,” the department said in a statement today.
It said the situation at Ranau Hospital reflected a broader shortage of medical officers across Sabah, with several other healthcare facilities facing similar challenges.
As an immediate measure, Sabah JKN will deploy three temporary relief medical officers, or ‘floater’ officers, to Ranau Hospital in stages, beginning on October 28 and November 11.
Meanwhile, the MOH will conduct a special permanent appointment exercise for Grade UD10 medical officers to meet the staffing needs of healthcare services in Sabah and Sarawak.
Sabah JKN said the placement of medical officers under the special exercise, with reporting for duty, was expected to begin as early as February 2027.
The department reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring the continuity of essential medical services while taking proactive measures to address the shortage of medical officers in the state. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: JKN stands for Jabatan Kesihatan Negeri in Malay.

Title: Brothers on opposite sides: Akmal Salleh's sibling stands for Bersama in Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Dr Muhammad Solehin Saleh, the elder brother of Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, is among 16 Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) candidates contesting the Melaka state election.
Muhammad Solehin, 40, is representing the party in the Bemban state seat under the Jasin parliamentary constituency in a four-cornered fight,
Sinar Harian
reported.
He will face Muhammad Rabaie Ab Hamid of Bersatu, Mohd Yadzil Yaakub of PN-Wawasan and independent candidate Abd Halim Said.
Muhammad Solehin is a medical doctor with a Bachelor of General Medicine from Universitas Sriwijaya, Indonesia.
Meanwhile, Akmal is defending the Merlimau seat for Barisan Nasional (BN) in a straight fight against Pakatan Harapan’s Rahayu Hamzah of Amanah.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, Akmal retained the seat for Umno-BN with a majority of 3,248 votes.
He was later appointed state executive councillor in charge of health before being moved to the rural development, agriculture and food security portfolio in 2023.

Title: Stolen Hilux leads cops to syndicate behind eight 4x4 thefts in Perak and KL
Article:
SITIAWAN, Oct 31 — Police have crippled a syndicate believed to be involved in stealing four-wheel-drive vehicles in Perak and Kuala Lumpur with the arrest of three people in Kampung Koh here on Tuesday.
Manjung district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hasbullah Abd Rahman said the arrests were made following information and intelligence gathered after a report on the theft of a Toyota Hilux in Taman Mas 2, Sitiawan, on Oct 26.
He said the Manjung district police headquarters received the report at about 10.06am that day.
“Following the report, a team from the Manjung district police headquarters arrested a man and two women suspected of being involved in the incident on Oct 27 at about 5.30pm.
“Police also seized a car key reader believed to have been used to steal vehicles, as well as several other items,” he said in a statement today,
Sinar Harian r
eported.
Hasbullah said questioning revealed the suspects had admitted to being involved in eight vehicle thefts using the same modus operandi, targeting four-wheel-drive vehicles.
He said four of the cases were reported in Perak and the other four in Kuala Lumpur.
According to the report, the case is being investigated under Section 379A of the Penal Code for motor vehicle theft, and all three suspects have been remanded for six days from Oct 28 to Nov 2.
Members of the public with information on the case are urged to come forward to the Manjung district police headquarters, contact its operations room at 05-688 6222, reach its WhatsApp hotline at 017-682 8005, or visit any nearby police station.

Title: Child, 10, among 181 detained in Chow Kit immigration raid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — The Immigration Department detained 181 foreign nationals for various immigration offences during an integrated operation at Jalan Raja Bot, or Chow Kit Market, here this morning.
Immigration Department deputy director-general (Operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli said the operation began at 9.40 am and involved checks on 512 foreign nationals.
“A total of 181 foreign nationals were detained for various immigration offences, including lacking valid travel documents, overstaying, and pass misuse,” he told reporters at the scene today.
He said those detained included 147 Indonesians, 20 Bangladeshis, five Nepalese, three Indians, one Pakistani and five others from various countries, aged between 10 and 55. All detainees were brought to the Bukit Jalil Immigration Depot for further action.
The integrated operation also involved Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL), the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN), the National Registration Department, the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department and the Royal Malaysia Police.
Lokman Effendi said Raja Bot Market is among 224 hotspots nationwide under continuous monitoring by the authorities.
He said this was the second operation at the location this year after intelligence gathering to determine the right time for an enforcement operation.
Operations will continue if immigration law violations persist, and no area will be exempt from enforcement, he said.
He added that enforcement actions are not limited to foreign nationals, as employers and premises owners who break the law will also face legal consequences.
“We remind employers not to commit any offences under the Immigration Act, as they will also be liable to legal action under this Act.
“Locals attempting to assist these foreign nationals can also be acted against, as harbouring undocumented foreign nationals in our country constitutes an offence,” he said.
Lokman Effendi said foreign nationals legally residing in the country need not worry, as enforcement operations target only those who violate the law. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: DBKL stands for Dewan Bandaraya Kuala Lumpur in Malay, while KPDN stands for Kementerian Perdagangan Dalam Negeri dan Kos Sara Hidup.

Title: Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir: MCA takes on DAP’s home turf
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 31 — Two additional state assembly seats to be contested by MCA candidates in the 16th Melaka state election, namely Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir, pose a significant challenge for the party to secure the people’s mandate in the state, especially from the Chinese community.
MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong said it serves as a platform to gauge public support for the party because the majority of voters in both constituencies are Chinese, and these seats have been dominated by the DAP for several terms.
Wee, who is also the Ayer Hitam member of parliament and a former transport minister, said that the Melaka state election is likened to a referendum to assess the people’s support for the Pakatan Harapan government, which has been governing the country for almost four years.
“We realise that it is not easy to conquer the two DAP strongholds, but we will work hard to gain the people’s mandate in these areas.
“We will make the best use of this opportunity by mobilising our efforts and machinery to gain the support of the voters,” he said after accompanying the Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate for the Kelebang state constituency, Datuk Lim Ban Hong, to the Nomination Centre at the State
Legislative Assembly Development and Coordination Committee Complex (Japerun).
Commenting on BN’s decision to grant the two additional seats to MCA, Wee said they appreciated the trust and support of the BN leadership as well as the views of the Perikatan Nasional (PN) leaders who deemed MCA suitable to contest and potentially win in those areas.
He said the MCA always pays attention to the people of Melaka, including all the state assembly constituencies under the Kota Melaka parliamentary constituency, even though the area is a stronghold of the DAP.
Meanwhile, he is confident that Lim can retain the Kelebang state assembly seat based on his excellent service record and good relationship with the local community, despite facing a rather intense four-cornered contest.
“We will continue to work hard to ensure that every vote from the people of Kelebang can be secured, thereby strengthening the position of the MCA,” he also said.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as the polling day for the Melaka state election, while the nomination of candidates is today and early voting is on November 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: Japerun stands for Jawatankuasa Pembangunan dan Penyelarasan Dewan Undangan Negeri in Malay.

Title: Pakatan has both ends of the age scale covered: A 24-year-old law grad and a retired captain, 66
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — The youngest candidate in the 16th Melaka state election, Muhammad Mukhlisul Mubin Julasapiyah, will contest the Kuala Linggi state seat.
Representing Pakatan Harapan (PH), the 24-year-old from Parti Amanah and a law graduate of Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia faces a three-cornered fight for the seat.
He will be challenged by incumbent Datuk Rosli Abdullah of Barisan Nasional (BN) and Dr Nur Farhana Hamzah of Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
In the 2021 Melaka polls, PH’s Farzana Hayani Nasir set the youngest-candidate record, at 21.
Kuala Linggi is one of five state seats under the Masjid Tanah parliamentary constituency, with 15,483 registered voters eligible to cast their ballots this time around.
Meanwhile, Capt (Rtd) Mohamad Jaafar, 66, also representing PH, is the oldest candidate in this election, contesting the Telok Mas seat against incumbent Datuk Abdul Razak Abdul Rahman of BN and Muhammad Hazwan Mustafa of Bersama.
The oldest candidate in the previous polls was Datuk Kalsom Noordin, 68, who contested the Pengkalan Batu seat on a BN ticket.
Telok Mas is one of five state seats under the Kota Melaka parliamentary constituency, with 29,751 eligible registered voters.
Of the 79 candidates in this election, 14 are women, a slight decline from the previous election, which saw 16 women among 112 candidates, with PH fielding the most female candidates at six.
The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day, with early voting on November 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Capt (Rtd) stands for Captain (Retired), or Kapten (Bersara) in Malay. Amanah is the short name for Parti Amanah Negara.

Title: Police arrest 16 foreigners in raid on Jalan Ampang hotel penthouse ‘mini casino’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Police have detained 16 foreign nationals after raiding a hotel penthouse on Jalan Ampang where a “mini casino” was operating.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Fadil Marsus said the raid was carried out at 1.50am today, according to a
Free Malaysia Today
report.
“An investigation found that the penthouse was being used as a mini casino open only to close acquaintances, involving Chinese nationals only,” he said in a statement.
Those arrested comprised 15 Chinese nationals, including one woman, and a Nepali, all aged between 26 and 50.
Police seized 214 poker chips valued at RM5,180 in total, along with RM1,000 in cash.
The case is being investigated under the Immigration Act, the Common Gaming Houses Act and Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing public servants.
The suspects are due to be brought to the magistrates’ court today for remand.

Title: Among the youngest in the race, Pakatan’s Nana says Kelebang needs a voice for women and young people
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 31 — Undeterred by her defeat in her first electoral contest in Sungai Rambai, Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir is once again throwing her hat into the ring in the 16th Melaka state election.
The 26-year-old Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate, affectionately known as Nana, said her unsuccessful electoral debut at 21 had been a valuable learning experience, giving her renewed confidence to contest the Kelebang state seat.
The Tangga Batu Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) chief said the experience had also given her a better understanding of the challenges involved, allowing her to prepare more effectively this time around.
“What I learnt from my first election has really helped me prepare for Kelebang. Alhamdulillah, we’re much more organised this time, especially with our schedules and campaign machinery,” she told reporters after the nomination process at the Klebang State Legislative Assembly Development and Coordination Committee (Japerun) Complex here today.
The Bukit Rambai native said she remained determined to give her best for voters in the constituency despite being the youngest candidate in a four-cornered contest.
Farzana Hayani said she would use the 14-day campaign period to champion women’s issues, while also focusing on the needs of the fishing community and job opportunities for young people.
“I understand the challenges of being a mother, a wife and a working woman. I also know how difficult it can be for young women who have to live apart from their husbands because of work,” she said.
Meanwhile, Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate Datuk Lim Ban Hong said he was taking nothing for granted in the state election despite being the incumbent Kelebang assemblyman.
The Melaka MCA chairman said he had never stopped working for his constituents and remained committed to serving the local community.
“This state election gives me another opportunity to continue working for the people of Kelebang and do my best for them. I hope they will once again give me and BN the mandate to continue serving them,” he said.
Farzana Hayani and Lim will face off against Bersatu’s Datuk Seri Mohamad Ali Mohamad and Parti Bersama Malaysia’s Young Jie Yu in the race for the Klebang state seat.
Polling day is set for November 14, with early voting on November 10.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Japerun stands for Jawatankuasa Pembangunan dan Penyelarasan Dewan Undangan Negeri in Malay while AMK refers to the youth wing of PKR.

Title: Same fix as 2023, please: Indian civil servants ask Putrajaya to add Nov 10 as extra Deepavali day
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 31 — The Putrajaya Indian Civil Servants Association (Imaiyam) is appealing to the government to grant unrecorded leave (CTR) to Hindu civil servants on Tuesday, November 10, as this year’s Deepavali leave overlaps with a public holiday and its replacement holiday.
Imaiyam chairman Dr Sathiskumar K. Muthusamy said the request is not aimed at securing a new benefit, but at ensuring that the existing Deepavali CTR, long provided by the government, can be fully enjoyed by Hindu civil servants.
“Deepavali this year falls on a Sunday, and Monday has been declared a replacement holiday. As a result, the day usually used for CTR overlaps with the public holiday, and the benefit cannot be enjoyed,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
“Our request is simple: that the CTR be allowed on Tuesday, November 10. The government made the same decision in 2023 under similar circumstances. We are confident it will remain consistent with that approach,” he said.
Dr Sathiskumar said the Deepavali CTR is already governed by the Human Resource Service Circular (MyPPSM); therefore, the Public Service Department (JPA) only needs to issue a circular letter allowing the CTR to be carried over to the next working day, as was done in 2023.
He said the circular could also be extended to state public services, statutory bodies and local authorities to ensure coordinated implementation.
Imaiyam has received questions and feedback from members about the limited time available during the Deepavali break, particularly among civil servants working far from their hometowns, including in Sabah and Sarawak.
“With only one replacement holiday, the time to return to one’s hometown, celebrate with family and return to work is very limited,” he said, adding that the matter has been brought to JPA’s attention.
Imaiyam stressed that fairness must underpin the consideration of festive leave for all civil servants regardless of religion or race.
If existing festive leave for followers of other religions is similarly affected by overlaps with public or replacement holidays, the same approach should be considered.
Since 2018, the government has provided one day of CTR for Deepavali, on the following day, to Hindu civil servants as an addition to the public holiday, giving them more room to celebrate with their families. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: CTR stands for Cuti Tanpa Rekod, MyPPSM refers to Pekeliling Perkhidmatan Sumber Manusia, and JPA stands for Jabatan Perkhidmatan Awam in Malay.
